Round 1 and round 2 were fix-round retests. They covered detector anchor classification (F-001, F-004, F-005), symlinked CLI entrypoints (F-003), and the narrow first-step diagram scale (F-002). The log and handoff say these were NOT exercised: the create/modify/repair agent journeys, all nine narrow steps, a wide screenshot matrix, and the touch/navigation matrix. They also say no automated suites were run. The reason given is that the diff was small and the acceptance skill prohibits suites. That is a candidate choice, not an environmental impediment. That leaves large areas of user-visible behavior with no acceptance observation. Each step uses the same Scene and the same groupKey. Stage.tsx keys the motion.div by step.groupKey ?? step.id inside a LayoutGroup, so one Scene instance stays mounted and only the payload changes. Stable identity runs through the presentation-owned ID constants in entities.ts. Newcomers enter through Appear, which spreads appearMotion onto its wrapper. The wrapper starts at opacity 0 and fades in with delay ENTER_DELAY. ENTER_DELAY equals LAYOUT_T, which is 0.6s. Continuing entities move through Entity&#39;s layout transition, which also lasts LAYOUT_T (0.6s) and has no delay. Continuing arrows animate their path d over LAYOUT_T with no delay. So a newcomer&#39;s visible entry starts only once the continuing layout motion has ended. The delay sits only on the Appear fade, not on the continuing layout motion. nodes.test.tsx asserts that the initial opacity is 0, that the delay is ENTER_DELAY, and that ENTER_DELAY &gt;= LAYOUT_T. All nine sample steps share one groupKey, so a single Scene instance persists. Every entity the sample adds on a beat after beat 1 is rendered inside a keyed Appear: interview, each card-i with its link and label, ghost/depth, socket, verify, modify and reveal. Judge A fails this because the &#39;you&#39; Box has no entry motion. That fact does not decide the requirement. The requirement covers a step that introduces an entity new relative to the steps before it, so persisting entities can settle first. The &#39;you&#39; Box is unconditional and is rendered on step 1 as part of the opening state, when there is no earlier step and nothing to settle. It is never newly rendered by any navigation: sample.test.tsx shows it keeps the same DOM node across all nine steps. The Stage&#39;s AnimatePresence also uses initial={false}, so the opening render plays no entrance for the scene. &#39;you&#39; is therefore never an entity a step transition introduces. Judges B and C reach the same conclusion, and the source bears it out.","evidence":["src/presentation-kit/constants.ts:6-8: LAYOUT_T = 0.6, ENTER_T = 0.4, ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T.","src/presentation-kit/nodes/appearMotion.ts:4-8: initial { opacity: 0 }; animate opacity 1 with transition delay ENTER_DELAY.","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Appear.tsx:12-17: the Appear motion.div spreads appearMotion onto the wrapper around newcomer children.","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Entity.tsx:23-26: motion.div with layout and layoutId={id}; its transition is duration LAYOUT_T with no delay. Judge A failed the criterion because the &#39;you&#39; Box has no entry motion. The detector followed only one level of delegation and reported `build: false`, `scaffold: full`. Is that a defect?"},{"line":2601,"text":""},{"line":2602,"text":"**Requirement:** `specs/presentation-skill/spec.md:25` and `:29`: the build anchor is a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`, and detection is contract-level so differences in organisation must not trigger re-scaffolding."},{"line":2603,"text":""},{"line":2604,"text":"**Ruling:** This is a defect, and I fixed it. It was a limit I introduced in the round 0 F-001 fix. `buildCommand` in `skills/presentation/scripts/detect-target.mjs` now follows `npm|pnpm|yarn|bun [run] <script>` delegation to any depth, with a visited set so script cycles terminate. The F-001 rejections still hold: `echo build`, `tsc -b` alone and cyclic scripts that never reach `vite` are not build anchors. A new unit test covers a three-level chain across npm and pnpm, and a cycle. It fails on the previous code and passes now."},{"line":2605,"text":""},{"line":2606,"text":"**Test results:** `evidence/acceptance-fix-round1-unit-tests.log` (detect-target and scaffold unit tests, 31 passed), `evidence/acceptance-fix-round1-unit-tests-prefix-code.log` (the new test failing on the previous code) and `evidence/acceptance-fix-round1-lint.log` (eslint clean)."},{"line":2607,"text":""},{"line":2608,"text":"**Integration/E2E assessment:** This is pure detection logic over fixture directories, which the unit tests cover fully. No integration test adds meaningful coverage. The detector followed only one level of delegation and reported `build: false`, `scaffold: full`. Is that a defect?"},{"line":2601,"text":""},{"line":2602,"text":"**Requirement:** `specs/presentation-skill/spec.md:25` and `:29`: the build anchor is a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`, and detection is contract-level so differences in organisation must not trigger re-scaffolding."},{"line":2603,"text":""},{"line":2604,"text":"**Ruling:** This is a defect, and I fixed it. It was a limit I introduced in the round 0 F-001 fix. `buildCommand` in `skills/presentation/scripts/detect-target.mjs` now follows `npm|pnpm|yarn|bun [run] <script>` delegation to any depth, with a visited set so script cycles terminate. The F-001 rejections still hold: `echo build`, `tsc -b` alone and cyclic scripts that never reach `vite` are not build anchors. A new unit test covers a three-level chain across npm and pnpm, and a cycle. It fails on the previous code and passes now."},{"line":2605,"text":""},{"line":2606,"text":"**Test results:** `evidence/acceptance-fix-round1-unit-tests.log` (detect-target and scaffold unit tests, 31 passed), `evidence/acceptance-fix-round1-unit-tests-prefix-code.log` (the new test failing on the previous code) and `evidence/acceptance-fix-round1-lint.log` (eslint clean)."},{"line":2607,"text":""},{"line":2608,"text":"**Integration/E2E assessment:** This is pure detection logic over fixture directories, which the unit tests cover fully. No integration test adds meaningful coverage. I did not run integration tests in this round, per instructions."},{"line":2609,"text":""},{"line":2610,"text":"**Limit, unchanged:** Detection stays static. It does not run the build, so a build script that reaches `vite` through something other than an npm-style script reference (for example a shell wrapper script) is still read as lacking the anchor. In a non-empty project that falls to the confirm-before-write step rather than overwriting anything."},{"line":2611,"text":""},{"line":2612,"text":"**Pending decision from the user:** F-005 is a different case: the cyclic script contains `vite build` but cannot reach it at runtime (`loop: &quot;npm run build &amp;&amp; vite build&quot;`, line 2373). The round-2 observation therefore exposes a new defect rather than disproving the ledger&#39;s statement. 2. The ledger itself warns that detection is static and cannot prove that `npm run build` works (lines 2554 and 2610). 3. The record states this exact gap as open finding F-005 in the log, the findings history and the handoff, so nothing is concealed and no stronger outcome is claimed than the evidence shows.","citations":["packet.txt"],"evidence":["Handoff lines 2266-2272: Acceptance NOT READY with F-002 and F-005 unresolved.","Handoff line 2294 discloses what was not exercised; line 2298 gives CI status and says build results are not a substitute for the suite.","Handoff line 2318 says compositions other than the narrow first scene lack current-pass visual evidence.","Log line 2252 and handoff line 2292 disclose the tester setup errors with cause and correction.","Findings lines 2369-2375 and log lines 2244-2250 record F-005 openly.","Ledger line 2604 refers to cycles that never reach vite; the F-005 fixture contains vite after the cycle, which is a separately disclosed defect.","Ledger line 2556 matches the logs at lines 3578-3579 (8 failed) and 3592 (30 passed); ledger line 2606 matches lines 2664 (1 failed) and 2677 (31 passed).","quoted lines: packet.txt:2264-2341","quoted lines: packet.txt:2345-2376","quoted lines: packet.txt:2380-2391","quoted lines: packet.txt:2224-2260","quoted lines: packet.txt:2598-2612","quoted lines: packet.txt:2634-2681","quoted lines: packet.txt:2552-2556","quoted lines: packet.txt:3708-3709","quoted lines: packet.txt:2781-2782","decider ruling: pass, confirmed by the closed-world span audit"]}}]},"assumption-handling":null}
dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[],"engineering-quality":[{"id":"engineering-preview-readiness-bounded","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The criterion requires that every wait for preview readiness has a timeout. In both copies of preview.mjs, the readiness wait in startPreview is a loop capped at 150 iterations with a 200 ms sleep between probes. It also checks on each iteration whether the child process has exited early, and it throws a &#39;did not become ready&#39; PhaseError once the retry budget runs out. So the readiness wait is bounded. The auditor argues instead that a single fetch could hang forever. That only happens if the local vite preview server accepts a connection and then never answers, and nothing in the source or recorded evidence shows that happening. The rubric says not to fail a criterion on a hypothetical scenario unless the review guidance names it, and this guidance does not name a hanging probe. The auditor itself agrees the other two clauses are met: the synchronous runBuild (spawnSync) finishes before startPreview in both verify scripts, and readiness polls over HTTP rather than parsing the server&#39;s printed ready URL. The stated reason therefore does not defeat the pass.","evidence":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs and the template copy: `for (let i = 0; i &lt; 150; i++) { if (exited) throw ...; try { const res = await fetch(`${url}/`); if (res.ok) return ... } catch {} await sleep(200) …","Readiness also stops early if the child exits: `if (exited) throw new PhaseError(&#39;preview&#39;, &#39;vite preview exited early...&#39;)`.","scripts/verify.mjs and the template copy call `runBuild(root)` (spawnSync, synchronous) before `await startPreview(root)`. The inspect scripts likewise build before previewing unless --skip-build is …","Readiness probes over HTTP with fetch and never parses stdout for a ready URL, so the ANSI/chunk clause does not apply.","A fetch that hangs only against a server that accepts connections but never responds is a hypothetical the cited source does not show, and the review guidance does not name it."],"citations":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs","scripts/verify.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":2,"sample":3},{"id":"engineering-typed-kit-primitives","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"The auditor&#39;s claim holds. The guidance fails a primitive that &quot;spreads caller props after setting its layoutId, entity identifier, or a data-presentation-* hook so a caller can override them.&quot; Box sets the hook value first and spreads caller props after it: `&lt;Entity kind=&quot;box&quot; {...rest}&gt;`. Entity then writes that value to the DOM as `data-presentation-node={kind}`. So if a caller&#39;s props contain `kind` at runtime, it replaces the fixed &#39;box&#39;. The type `Omit&lt;EntityProps,&#39;kind&#39;|...&gt;` does not prevent this: it gives no runtime protection, and a JSX spread of a wider object is not checked for extra properties. Label (`kind=&quot;label&quot; {...props}`), Frame (`kind=&quot;frame&quot; inert {...rest}`), SymbolChip (`kind=&quot;chip&quot; {...rest}`) and Emphasis (`kind=&quot;emphasis&quot; ... {...rest}`) use the same order. The repository and bootstrap copies are identical. This is the exact ordering the guidance names as failing, so the identity-protection clause is unmet and the pass verdict does not hold.","evidence":["src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx: `export function Box({ Icon, label, children, ...rest }: BoxProps) { return ( &lt;Entity kind=&quot;box&quot; {...rest}&gt;`","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Entity.tsx: `data-presentation-node={kind}` and `data-presentation-id={id}` are set from the received props","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Label.tsx: `return &lt;Entity kind=&quot;label&quot; {...props} /&gt;`","src/presentation-kit/nodes/SymbolChip.tsx: `&lt;Entity kind=&quot;chip&quot; {...rest}&gt;`; Frame.tsx: `&lt;Entity kind=&quot;frame&quot; inert {...rest}&gt;`","The bootstrap template copies under skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentation-kit/nodes/ contain the same code"],"citations":["src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Entity.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Label.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Frame.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/SymbolChip.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Emphasis.tsx","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentation-kit/nodes/Entity.tsx","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentation-kit/nodes/Label.tsx"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":2,"sample":3}],"testing-evidence":[],"assumption-handling":[]}
